title: Wait for a Human Without Losing the Workflow
description: A booking workflow can wait 24 hours for fraud review, and its worker may restart during that time. Which design preserves progress and bounds held resources?

options.text: Keep the review state only in the worker's memory.
options.explanation: A restart loses the pending decision and leaves the system unable to resume reliably.

options.text: Hold a database transaction open throughout review.
options.explanation: Long-held locks and connections couple availability to human response time and do not suit independent services.

options.text: Persist workflow history and a durable timer, await a review signal, then compensate or escalate on timeout.
options.explanation: A durable workflow engine can recover the wait after restart. An explicit timeout policy prevents indefinite reservations; activities still need idempotency.

options.text: Replay the whole workflow with fresh payment keys after each restart.
options.explanation: Fresh keys can repeat committed side effects instead of recovering their recorded outcomes.
